correctness.rationale: For bounded type, frequencies in 2^r≤|k|<2^(r+1) are separated modulo one by at least cα/2^(r+2), and individually stay at least cα/2^(r+1) from zero. Using the weaker separation constant covers opposite signs in RESULT.md:39 without changing its estimate. The j-th smallest distance is bounded below by a constant times j·2^(-r); thus the reciprocal-square sum is O(2^(2r)). Weighted Cauchy–Schwarz then makes the transfer's Fourier coefficients summable for s>1, with the zero coefficient handled by the mean-zero hypothesis and conjugate symmetry giving a real continuous transfer. At s=1 the chosen positive convergent errors obey q_jδ_j bounded above and away from zero and the ratios of q_j bounded above and away from one. H_a is in L² and the translated difference is uniformly convergent with H¹ energy comparable to Σa_j². Positive divergent Fejér means at zero exclude even an essentially bounded transfer, since measurable transfers differ only by an invariant constant. The split at 1/h gives the upper modulus h(A_J+O(a_{J+1})); at h_j=1/(8q_j) the first j increments have one sign and magnitude in total at least c h_j A_j while the geometric tail is O(h_j a_{j+1}). For intervening h, choose consecutive h_{j+1}≤h<h_j: h_{j+1} is comparable to h and J(h) differs from j+1 by a bounded index, so monotonicity gives the lower estimate for all small h. Taking a_j=1/j yields h log log(1/h). For arbitrary nondecreasing divergent L, recursively make each block long enough to reach L(q_{N_{m+1}})≥(m+1)², with nondecreasing lengths at least 2^m. Unit mass per block gives a_j nonincreasing in ℓ² but not ℓ¹ and A_J=o(L(q_J)), as required. Read RESULT.md:3–77, VERIFICATION.md and verify_rotation.py; did not execute submitted code. The proof, not finite truncations at the golden rotation, establishes the general assertion.

evidence: The positive Sobolev direction uses a standard weighted divisor-sum argument. A C¹ obstruction would imply the upper gauge claim simultaneously for every divergent L, since its modulus is O(h). There is also a direct nonconstructive reduction: a universal continuous transfer for mean-zero C¹ data would, by the closed graph theorem on continuous mean-zero derivatives and normalized continuous solutions, make evaluation of the transfer at zero a finite-measure multiplier m(k)=[2πik(e^(2πikα)−1)]⁻¹. Along convergents pass to a subsequence with m(q_j)→m*≠0; m(q_j+k)→0 for each fixed k≠0. Hence modulation of that measure by e^(2πiq_jx) would converge weakly to m* times Lebesgue measure. Its absolutely continuous part tends weakly to zero by Riemann–Lebesgue, while limits of the modulated singular part are dominated by the same singular total variation measure, a contradiction. Bounded type ensures an L² transfer for every H¹ datum. This implication check is independent reasoning, not an attribution to an unread source.

value.rationale: The exact Sobolev boundary identifies which mean-zero rotation data always have continuous transfer. The worthwhile quantitative addition is an explicit family for every angle in scope with a two-sided modulus on all small scales and an L² transfer whose unboundedness is provable. Prescribing very slow but divergent excess over the Lipschitz scale inside a single tractable family is stronger information than a qualitative obstruction or an upper bound alone.
